newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - EMU and rate talk buoy gilt, short stg vols.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - EMU and rate talk buoy gilt, short stg vols.

text.p: Implied volatility of gilt and short sterling options ticked higher on Monday as politics and interest rates came into focus, brokers said.

Traders said news that a split had widened within in the ruling Conservative party over European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) and the prospect of a monetary meeting scheduled for later this session were keeping vols bid up.
"Gilts have been pretty quiet but short sterling has seen quite a bit of business," said one options broker on London's LIFFE floor.
He said vols were slightly higher in both markets.

December gilt options were trading at an implied vol of 6.62 to 6.76 percent versus 6.22 percent on Friday, while March implied vol was quoted at 6.71 and 6.88 percent, up from 6.57 percent on Friday.
"We saw some people trading out of straddle positions (in gilt options) during the October expiry this morning, but apart from that there has been very little traded," the broker said.

In the short sterling options market, traders said business was a bit more lively with a few prominent so-called "Eurosceptics" within the government calling for Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke to "consider his position".
Clarke said at the weekend that he would not rule out membership of the single European currency despite attempts by the "Eurosceptics" within his party to spark a "civil war" on the issue.

"We had quite a flurry (in short sterling options) this morning," said one LIFFE options trader for a U.S. bank. "Implied vols were all over the place for a while but now they seem to have settled down again."
LIFFE screens showed 700 lots in March 93.75 short sterling puts had gone through the market by 1100 GMT.
In calls, 835 lots of December 93.50 strikes, 780 lots of 94.00 strikes and 374 lots of 94.25 strikes had been traded.
